text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bunds extended their gains in late dealings, hitting fresh contract highs after a surprising drop in U.S. September jobs data. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.73, up 0.59 from the previous settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts secured almost another point on Friday, tracking euphoric U.S. Treasuries, buoyed by a shock 40,000 fall in the September non-farm payroll. But dealers said the market will run into profit-taking next week and warn the Conservative Party Conference could take some of the shine of gilts' performance. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-28/32, up 31/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bonds wrapped up a week-long rally with the December futures contract just shy of yet another high struck after U.S. payroll data stunned the market and sent U.S. and European debt soaring. The market is geared up for a further advance next week, traders and analysts said. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 125.90, up 0.48 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt futures closed almost unchanged from Thursday after a roller-coaster ride, spiking upwards when U.S. data showed a surprise drop in jobs, then going into a dive as hedge funds took profits and switched into Bunds. Market-watchers said BTPs could face a further correction next week with many funds sitting on fat profits after a robust bull run, although a major fall was seen as unlikely. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.19, up 0.14 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries advanced. The 30-year bond yield overcame resistance at 6.75 percent, briefly dipping to 6.73 percent, with bond prices rising after a surprise 40,000 drop in U.S. September jobs. Technical buying buoyed the market after yields dipped below 6.75 percent. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-22/32, up 1/12/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.74 percent.

JAPAN - December Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) ended at a new contract high of 122.83. One- to two-year sector of cash JGB market strongest in yield curve. City banks actively purchased two-year fixed interest rates in swap market. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 123.22, up 0.52 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Korea Development Bank launched a debut 1.5 billion French franc six-year Eurobond. Sweden tapped the market twice, with a N$150 million two-year issue and a 17.5 billion yen one-year deal redeemable in New Zealand dollars.
